title: Mean of the normal approximation to a Poisson variable
source: Theory S2-2.4 Quick check 1 (Po(50) is approximated by N(50, 50), mean 50); new large integer means
stem: The random variable \(X\) has the distribution \(\mathrm{Po}({n|int})\). A normal distribution is used as an approximation to this Poisson distribution. What is the mean of the approximating normal distribution?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: The approximating distribution is \(\mathrm{N}({n|int}, {n|int})\), so the mean is {A|int}.
steps.note: A equals n. Original n=50 gives mean 50.

title: Variance of the normal approximation to a Poisson variable
source: Theory S2-2.4 Quick check 2 (the variance of the approximating N(50, 50) is 50); new large integer means
stem: The random variable \(X\) has the distribution \(\mathrm{Po}({n|int})\). A normal distribution is used as an approximation. What is the variance of the approximating normal distribution?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: For a Poisson distribution the variance equals the mean, so the approximating distribution is \(\mathrm{N}({n|int}, {n|int})\) and the variance is {A|int}.
steps.note: A equals n. Original n=50 gives variance 50.

title: Continuity-corrected boundary for P(X less than k)
source: Theory S2-2.4 Quick check 3 (P(X<36) is approximated by P(Y<35.5)); new integer cut-offs
stem: The Poisson random variable \(X\) is approximated by a continuous normal random variable \(Y\). The probability \(\mathrm{P}(X\lt {k|int})\) is approximated by \(\mathrm{P}(Y\lt c)\). What is the value of \(c\)?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: With a continuity correction, \(X\lt {k|int}\) is replaced by \(Y\lt {k|int}-0.5\), so \(c={A|dp1}\).
steps.note: A is k-0.5. Original k=36 gives 35.5.

title: Normal approximation to the number of people arriving in one hour

source.note: Stem taken from the QP PDF (UCLES 2016), the opening sentence of Question 7 together with part (ii) only. Official answer and mark allocation from the MS PDF. The item is paper/self-mark. Part (i) is an exact Poisson calculation for a 5-minute period and is omitted (it is not the normal approximation).

stem:
This question is 9709/73/O/N/16 Question 7(ii), taken from the official QP.

Men arrive at a clinic independently and at random, at a constant mean rate of 0.2 per minute. Women arrive at the same clinic independently and at random, at a constant mean rate of 0.3 per minute.

(ii) Find the probability that fewer than 36 people arrive at the clinic during a 1-hour period.  [5]

steps.name: L
steps.text_tex: The combined mean rate is \(0.5\) people per minute, so in 60 minutes the mean is \(\lambda=30\).

steps.name: N
steps.note: Official MS 7(ii): B1, seen or implied, need N(lambda, lambda).

steps.name: Z
steps.text_tex: With a continuity correction, \(\mathrm{P}(X\lt 36)=\mathrm{P}(Y\lt 35.5)\), and the standardised value is \((35.5-30)/\sqrt{30}=1.004\ldots\).
steps.note: Official MS 7(ii): M1 for (35.5-30)/sqrt(30), allow with wrong or no continuity correction or no square root. Independent: 5.5/sqrt(30)=1.004158...

steps.name: F
steps.note: Official MS 7(ii): M1 for Phi of their standardised value, consistent with their working.

steps.name: A
steps.note: Official MS 7(ii): A1 for 0.842 (3 s.f.). Independent: Phi(1.004158...)=0.8424..., which is 0.842 to 3 s.f.
